subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification — shared vs dedicated isolation & SLOs
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finserv.io>, Olivia Barnes <olivia@retailco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Deployment mode follow-up — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Samir / Olivia,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Call recap:
- Primary goal: embed high-volume document-summarization + redaction into FinServ’s customer support pipeline.
- Traffic profile: peak ~150 QPS during business hours, baseline ~30 QPS.
- Latency target: P95 <= 200ms for short summaries (~150 tokens).
- Compliance: SOC 2 + data residency in us-east region; potential need for private VPC or on-prem for regulated data.
- Concern raised: noisy-neighbor interference on shared pools — want isolation guarantees and predictable SLOs.

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll put together two recommended deployment options (Dedicated pool vs Private VPC) with rough cost and timeline.
2) Marissa (SE) will detail isolation controls, autoscaling behavior, and how we meet your SLOs.
3) If acceptable, run a 2–3 week PoC on a dedicated pool to validate latency/throughput under your workload.
4) We’ll provide a draft SLA and baseline configuration for procurement.

I’ve attached a simple production architecture diagram and a draft SLO doc to start the discussion. 
Questions for you to confirm before we size the Dedicated pool:
- Can you share a small sample of the traffic distribution (percent of short vs long prompts, avg tokens)?
- Any hard restrictions on cold-start times or fallback behavior?

I’ll follow up with Marissa for the infra notes and a ballpark estimate.

Thanks — Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: prod-arch-diagram.png, slo-draft.pdf

From: Samir Shah <samir@finserv.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Olivia Barnes <olivia@retailco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole>
Date: 2027-04-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up — post-call recap and next steps

Priyom — thanks for the clear recap. Couple clarifications from our side: 

- The 150 QPS is what we see at peak after batching at the gateway; per-request concurrency to model will be ~40–60 concurrent model contexts.
- Prompt distribution: ~70% short (<= 200 tokens), 30% long (200–1,200 tokens).
- P95 <= 200ms is our target for the short prompts; for long ones we’re OK with higher but want stability.
- Noise concerns: we’ve had prior outages on shared clusters at other vendors where noisy tenants spiked latency. We need either strict isolation or strong, measurable fallbacks.
- Compliance: SOC 2 plus encryption-at-rest with customer KMS.

Budget note: procurement will need a ballpark OPEX estimate to evaluate Dedicated vs Private. If you can surface a 12-month run-rate for both options that will speed internal approvals.

We’re good with a PoC — preferred to start on Dedicated if the cost delta isn’t >35% vs shared+isolation.

Samir
Head of Platform Engineering, FinServ Inc.

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>

Great — thanks Samir. I’ll get Marissa and Vivek to scope the Dedicated vs Private numbers (12-month run-rate) and a proposed PoC plan.

Immediate asks for sizing: if you can share a 24-hour sample of request sizes or a small CSV with timestamp, token_count, and latency from your gateway that’d be ideal. Otherwise we’ll run with the profile you gave.

What we’ll provide by EOD Wednesday:
- Two configuration recommendations: Dedicated pool (isolated GPU farm, autoscale/burst policy) and Private VPC (customer-managed network + dedicated control plane).
- Ballpark pricing (monthly and 12-month commit) and expected time-to-deploy.
- PoC plan: 2–3 weeks on a dedicated pool, acceptance criteria focused on P95 latency and error rate.

Attached the prod-arch-diagram.png and slo-draft.pdf again so Marissa/Vivek can annotate.

Thanks — Priyom

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finserv.io>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Olivia Barnes <olivia@retailco.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni>
Date: 2027-04-26T10:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up — isolation, noisy neighbors, and SLOs (technical details)

Hi Samir / Olivia — Marissa here (SE). Wanted to surface technical details on how Redwood addresses the noisy-neighbor problem and how we’d meet your SLOs for the Dedicated and Private options.

Dedicated pool (recommended first step for validation):
- Isolation: Dedicated GPU nodes reserved for FinServ; no other tenants on those nodes. This eliminates cross-tenant scheduling interference.
- Autoscaling & burst: Configure baseline nodes for steady throughput and a short burst buffer for transient spikes. Bursts are handled via pre-warmed runners to avoid cold-starts.
- QoS & admission control: Request prioritization and backpressure to keep P95 latency stable; configurable per-route concurrency limits.
- Monitoring & alerting: Token-level latency breakdowns, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rates, and end-to-end P95/P99. We can export metrics to your Prometheus/Grafana or push to our Console.
- SLA: We provide an SLA for uptime and latency tiers on Dedicated pools; draft attached (redwood-dedicated-sla.docx).

Private VPC (if regulatory isolation required):
- All of the above plus customer-managed networking, KMS integration for encryption-at-rest, and optional on-prem package.
- Slightly longer lead time for setup (~4–6 weeks) vs Dedicated (~1–2 weeks) depending on networking and KMS approvals.

PoC plan (recommended):
- Duration: 2–3 weeks on a small Dedicated pool configured to FinServ profile; objective to validate P95 <= 200ms for short prompts at 150 QPS.
- Acceptance criteria: P95 latency target met for 3 consecutive business days and error rate <0.5%.
- Data handling: For regulated data we can route sensitive requests to a masked pipeline or use customer-managed KMS in Private VPC.

Next steps from our side:
- I’ll prepare a short configuration options doc and a pricing ballpark.
- If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-min technical kickoff to align on traffic shaping and test harness (I recommend including one of your SREs).

Linking the draft SLO and a quick runbook for PoC: https://docs.redwood.ai/pocts/RSW-3491-plan

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sla.docx

Samir
